title: Signal degradation attribution and automated rollback playbook for cross-cohort canaries
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: During staged rollouts (canary / A-B / shadow blends) we sometimes observe quality regressions that are hard to attribute to a particular cohort, prompt-set, or kernel optimization. Existing scorecard alerts fire, but engineers spend hours correlating signals across cohorts, prompt fingerprints, and token-level divergences to decide whether to rollback. Goal: deliver an automated attribution layer and a documented rollback playbook that reduces time-to-action and enables safe automated partial rollback decisions for clearly attributable degradations. Scope: 1) Build a lightweight attribution pipeline that maps failing eval prompts to cohorts, model variants, and kernel/quantization changes. 2) Produce a deterministic 'forensic delta' artifact per alert (fingerprint diff + token-level heatmap + affected customer cohorts). 3) Implement an auto-rollback policy that can be configured per project with hysteresis and manual approval gates. Out of scope: global model repro training or changes to model training loops.
acceptance_criteria: Forensic delta artifact is generated for >= 95% of eval-scorecard alerts within 3 minutes of alerting
Attribution confidence score (0-100) produced and logged; >= 80 confidence automatically qualifies for staged rollback per project policy
UI shows cohort-level impact and top-10 contributing prompts in Console rollout page
Playbook docs and runbook created with step-by-step manual rollback and escalation procedures
A/B and shadow blend tests include attribution metadata in telemetry payloads for 100% of traffic during rollout windows
proposed_solution: 1) Enrich scorecard pipeline: when a golden-prompt deviation threshold is crossed, spawn a lightweight attribution job that computes: prompt fingerprint diff, token-level divergence heatmap, and cohort impact summary using sampled traces. 2) Attribution engine computes a confidence score using heuristics: prompt overlap, token divergence magnitude, cohort isolation (only one cohort changed), and temporal correlation with deploy. 3) Persist a forensic-delta JSON artifact to S3 and index a small summary into the Console for quick triage. 4) Implement an Auto-Rollback Orchestrator that evaluates policies (thresholds, cooldown windows, manual approval requirements) and can either 1) flip traffic back for a specific cohort (e.g., revert canary to previous model) or 2) quarantine traffic to a fallback variant. 5) Expose controls in Console: set per-project rollback policy, view forensic artifact, and manually approve/abort automated actions.
design_decisions: Use deterministic prompt fingerprinting (prefix+hash of normalized prompt) rather than ML clustering to keep costs low and explainability high
Attribution uses conservative aggregation windows (5-15 minutes) to avoid transient noise causing rollbacks
Auto-rollback only allowed for high-confidence, single-cohort attributions; multi-cohort or low-confidence incidents go to manual triage
Forensic artifacts are immutable and stored for 90 days to support post-mortem analysis
Keep the initial engine as a separate microservice behind the existing eval pipeline to minimize risk to production traffic
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (infra + pipeline): instrument scorecard alerts to spawn attribution jobs; store forensic artifacts (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (Console + visibility): surface artifacts in rollout UI and add per-project policy controls (1 week)
Phase 3 (policy pilot): enable automated rollback for two low-risk internal projects with manual approval required; run for 2 weeks
Phase 4 (gradual expansion): enable fully automated rollback for projects with agreed SLAs and high test coverage; monitor false positives closely
Phase 5 (post-mortem cadence): weekly review of all auto-rollbacks and tuning of heuristics
metrics_and_alerts: Attribution precision / false-positive rate: target FP < 3% in pilot projects
Number of auto-rollbacks per week: monitor and cap by policy
Mean time to rollback decision (manual): target < 15m when triage required
Customer-visible error or regression rate delta (post-rollback): tracked per cohort
